In these example use cases, the testing revealed several gaps in the SOC team's requirements that
were established as baselines for the responsibilities of each team. The use case checklist can be as
comprehensive as needed to ensure that the SOC team is prepared for the Microsoft Defender XDR
integration with new or existing SOC requirements. Since this is an iterative process, the use case
development process and the use case output content naturally serve to update and mature the
SOC's runbooks with lessons learned.
Once use case testing has been remediated for all gaps, the lessons learned and metrics collected in
them can be incorporated into your SOC team's production runbooks (operating processes) and
playbooks (incident responses and escalation procedures).
Maintenance of the SOC team runbooks and playbooks can be organized in a multitude of ways. Each
SOC team may be responsible for their own, or there may be a single centralized version for all teams
to share in a central repository. Runbook and playbook management for individual organizations is
